MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 25, 2020
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:00 p.m., on August 25, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on August 20, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Karen Hamman, Director of Community Relations

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. City Representation of Legal Services: Public Employee Appointment and Public
  Employment: City Attorney Position.

City Council Minutes  1  August 25, 2020
 CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: Two
  (2) potential cases.

CS3. Liability Claims and Existing Litigation: Claimants: Donaldson, O’Brien, Peterson and
  Cunningham: Agency Claimed Against-City of Mission Viejo and: Significant
  Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9
  (4 cases).

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were three Closed Session items. The first will be
addressed with agenda item 21 regarding legal services. The second matter was consideration of
entering into a tolling agreement in regards to a landfill remediation which the City Council
approved and will execute and deliver to the plaintiff parties. Lastly, the Council was provided
updates on various claims filed against the City but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Goodell

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Juan Araiza, M.V.: Asked for the reopening of youth sports and questioned what the City’s protocol
will be.

Cynthia Cantrelle, M.V.: Asked that the City Council consider adopting a resolution proclaiming
that the City is a sanctuary for the unborn child.

Karla Navarro, Orange County: Requested that the City Council allow for live public comments
during Council Meeting or consider a live broadcast outside of City Hall.

Alexandra Macias, M.V.: Expressed her opposition to the extension of the terms of Council
Members Raths, Sachs, and Bucknum.

Arya Jemal, M.V.: Requested that the City Council allow for live public comments during Council
Meetings or consider a live broadcast outside of City Hall. She also stated that the City must
implement district voting.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated her belief that the City was in violation of the Ralph M. Brown Act at
the July 14, 2020, meeting in regards to item #17, Legal Services. She said that the public was not
allowed to make comments prior to the item being approved.

City Council Minutes  2  August 25, 2020
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 21 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Minutes of August 25, 2020, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated July 3, 2020 in the Amount of $1,351,937.57

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated July 10, 2020 in the Amount of $628,568.59

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated July 17, 2020 in the Amount of $976,167.08

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated July 24, 2020 in the Amount of $504,196.36

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated July 31, 2020 in the Amount of $847,506.49

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Check Register Dated August 7, 2020 in the Amount of $3,867,506.33

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending June 30, 2020

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending June
  30, 2020.

9.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2020

  Received and filed.
City Council Minutes  3  August 25, 2020
 10. Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for June 2020

  Received and filed.

11. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for June 2020

  Received and filed.

12. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2020

  Received and filed.

13. Annual Maintenance Program for the Repair and Reconstruction of Streets, Drainage
  Channels, Storm Drains, Slopes, Emergency Response and Heavy Equipment

  (1) Approved Sixth Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Bistline
  Engineering, Inc. for the subject services, and (2) authorized issuance of a contract change
  order in the amount not to exceed $85,000.00.

14. Lower Curtis Park (CIP 20245)

  (1) Approved the award of contract for permitting services to Glenn Lukos Associates (A20-
  23) in the amount of $76,520 for Lower Curtis Park; and (2) adopted Resolution 20-35
  Amending the Fiscal Year 2020/2021 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement
  Project 20245.

15. 2020 Residential Resurfacing - Slurry Seal (CIP 21838)

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Roy Allan Slurry Seal, Inc., (A20-
  24) in the amount of $492,550.70.

16. Transfer of Southern California Edison Rule 20A Allocations

  Authorized the City Manager to enter into an agreement with the City of Newport Beach
  (A20-25) to transfer the City's unused Rule 20A allocation of $47,766.00 within the Southern
  California Edison (SCE) Service Area to the City of Newport Beach in exchange for
  compensation in the amount of $26,271.30.

17. MV Shuttle - Cooperative Agreement and Deferral of Contract Renewal

  (1) Approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-0-2389 between the Orange County
  Transportation Authority (A20-26) and the City of Mission Viejo for Project V Community-
  Based Transit/Circulators; and (2) authorized the City Manager to Approve Amendment 1 to
  Contract A19-49 with LAZ Parking California, Inc. for the operation of the MV Shuttle.

18. Amending the City of Mission Viejo Authorized Position Schedule

City Council Minutes  4  August 25, 2020
   Adopted Resolution 20-36 Amending the City's Authorized Position Schedule Effective
  August 25, 2020.

19. First Amendment to Contract Agreement with City’s Independent Auditing Firm, Davis
  Farr LLP

  Approved Amendment to Contract Agreement with Davis Farr LLP, to Modify the Scope of
  work to Include additional Agreed Upon Procedures.

20. Modifications to the current Mission Viejo Nadadores Financial Relief due to the Covid-
  19 Outbreak

  Provided an additional 5 months for a total 10-month deferment of the $6,608.20 monthly
  payment for a total deferment of $66,082. The deferral amount would be added to the end of
  the 240- month term and the revised length of the loan term will be 250 months.

21. Agreement for Legal Services between the City of Mission Viejo and the law firm Harper
  & Burns LLP

  Approved the agreement with Harper & Burns LLP (A20-27) for Legal and City Attorney
  Services.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM CONSENT CALENDAR

21. Agreement for Legal Services between the City of Mission Viejo and the law firm Harper
  & Burns LLP

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve
  the agreement with Harper & Burns LLP for Legal and City Attorney Services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

22.  Public Hearing to Consider All Objections to the Proposed Abatement of Weeds on
  Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed Abatement Program 2020

  City Attorney Bill Curley gave the staff report.

  Mayor Goodell opened the Public Hearing at 6:28 p.m. Upon hearing no requests to speak,
  the Mayor closed the Public Hearing.

City Council Minutes  5  August 25, 2020
   Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to instruct
  the Public Services Department to proceed and perform the removal of weeds in accordance
  with Sections 39568 through 39588 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

23. General Plan Amendment GPA2020-33 / Zone Change ZC2020-23 / Planned
  Development Permit PDP2020-313 / Variance VAR2020-55 / and Tentative Tract Map
  TTM19035 - Petitions submitted by Trumark Homes to permit residential development
  on 6.36 acres of a 13.4-acre open space site located on El Toro Road, between Marguerite
  Parkway and the State Route 241 Toll Road (APN 839-273-04 and partial area of APN
  839-273-03). The subject property would be rezoned from R (Recreation) to RPD 30
  (Residential Planned Development) to accommodate a new residential project with 91
  for-sale dwelling units, clustered in ten 3-story buildings, with an overall project density
  of 14.3 du/ac. Variance VAR2020-55 is Requested to Allow Reduced Distance Between
  Buildings and Alternative Parking Space Configurations Including Both Tandem and
  Unenclosed Resident Parking

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister provided the staff report.

  Applicant Eric Nelson of Trumark Homes presented his report on the project.

  Mayor Goodell opened the Public Hearing at 6:54 p.m.

  The following provided written comments in support of the project: Janice Shackle, M.V.;
  Larry Christensen, M.V.; Elizabeth Hansburg, People for OC Housing; Kathleen and Terry
  Roach, M.V.; Kate Keena, former resident; Deborah Cottle, Building Industry Association
  Member; Tina Price, M.V.: Laer Pearce; Sherry Butterfield, M.V.; Christina Wollin, M.V.;
  Barbara Thomas, Rancho Santa Margarita; Rita Taenaka, M.V.; Dennis O’Connor, M.V;
  Jamie Hutcheon, M.V.; Buddy Owens, M.V.; Cathy Batesole, M.V.; Marilyn Schroeder,
  M.V.; John Achee, M.V.; Cynthia Russell, M.V.; Eileen Oldroyd, M.V.; Steve LaMotte,
  Building Industry Association Member; Samuel Cruz, M.V.; Michael Conte, M.V.; Roger
  Faubel, M.V.; Jane Haninger, M.V.; Derek Spalding, M.V.; Peter Vanek, Building Industry
  Association Member; Donna Varner, M.V.; and William Inghram, Rockwell Land Co.

  The following provided written comments in opposition to the project: Cynthia Bolin, M.V.;
  Nancy Varner, M.V.; Ken Bailey, M.V.; and Maggie Peters, M.V.

  The following called in to the meeting to state support for the project: Greg Powers, M.V.;
  Barbara Thomas, Rancho Santa Margarita; James O’Malley, M.V.; Julia Malisos, M.V.; Steve
  LaMotte, Huntington Beach; Rana Muncy, M.V.; Braden Carver, M.V.; Elizabeth Hansburg,
  People for Housing; Eileen Oldroyd, M.V.; and Buddy Owens, M.V.

City Council Minutes  6  August 25, 2020
   The following called in to the meeting to state opposition to the project: Nancy Varner, M.V.;
  and Maggie Peters, M.V.

  Lucy Meyer, M.V.: expressed concerns and asked questions about weed abatement issues on
  the property.

  There being no further public comments, Mayor Goodell closed the Public Hearing at 8:32
  p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 20-37 Approving General Plan Amendment GPA2020-33 and Adopting the
  Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration prepared for the project; (2) introduce
  Ordinance 20-339 Approving Zone Change ZC2020-23, Being a Petition Submitted by
  Trumark Homes to change the Zoning Map Designation from R (Recreation) to RPD 30
  (Residential Planned Development), for 6.36 Acres of Property Located on El Toro Road,
  Between Marguerite Parkway and the State Route 241 Toll Road, and further described as
  assessor parcel number 839-273-04 and 839-273-03 (portion)"; and (3) adopt Resolution 20-
  38 Approving Planned Development Permit PDP2020-313, Variance VAR2020-55, and
  Tentative Tract Map TTM19035.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

24. Authorization Resolution for Application and Receipt of SB 2 Permanent Local Housing
  Allocation Grant in the amount of $206,683 to provide funding assistance for Mercy
  House and a Homeless Liaison Officer

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to adopt
  Resolution 20-39 Authorizing Application for, and Receipt of, SB 2 Permanent Local
  Housing Allocation Grant in the Amount of $206,683 to Provide Funding Assistance for
  Mercy House and a Homeless Liaison Officer.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

25.  Small Business Grant Relief Program

City Council Minutes  7  August 25, 2020
   Planning & Economic Development Assistant Sarah McMillan presented the staff report.

  Council Member Sachs complimented Sarah for reaching out to businesses regarding this
  grant program.

  The City Council received and filed the report.

26.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Site C

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon gave the staff report.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that the City does not own this property as it was sold to the
  Housing Authority in 2015 for the purpose of removing the responsibility of creating housing
  opportunities from the City to the Housing Authority. She questioned why the City is getting
  re-involved in this property and expending general fund monies.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to adopt
  Resolution 20-40 Amending the Fiscal Year 2020/2021 Budget to Create Capital
  Improvement Project 21248 for Mission Viejo Housing Authority Site C Grading.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

27. Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the 2020 League of California Cities Annual
  Conference

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
  the Mayor’s appointment of Council Member Sachs as voting delegate and himself and
  Council Member Bucknum as alternates for the League of California Cities Conference
  Annual Business Meeting on October 9, 2020.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

28. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley continued her report to the next meeting.

29. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commissioner (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum held her report for the next meeting.
City Council Minutes  8  August 25, 2020
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

30. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum commented that she had a great summer and is enjoying the patio at the
Casta del Sol Golf Course. She commended City Staff for their work on the City’s trails and noted
that the trees that have been trimmed around the Lake. Council Member Bucknum gave kudos to
recreation department staff for slowly and safely reopening certain facilities. Lastly, she encouraged
businesses to reach out to City staff and the Chamber of Commerce for resources.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths stated that it has been a trying summer and he appreciates all the work that
staff has done during the pandemic. He noted that the schools went back into session virtually and
it upsets him to see his granddaughter schooling at home and the challenges that parents are facing
with children learning remotely. He also shared that he went to his dry cleaners only to find out
they went out of business. Council Member Raths encouraged residents to come together as a
community and stated that he hopes the curve will stay flat so schools can reopen soon. He thanked
the Mayor for all he has done this summer and thanked staff for the great presentation on the new
development that was discussed tonight. Finally, he asked staff for an update on the I-5 Widening
Project at the next meeting in September.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs also commented that it has been a tough summer. He spoke with an
individual in the economic development area at Saddleback College to inquire about putting
together an overview of the effect of business closures in the City in an effort to understand what
the City can do to bring these businesses back. He gave a shout out to Hatam Restaurant for
accommodating him for a meeting and he encouraged residents to check them out. Council Member
Sachs commented on the pension valuation report that was on the agenda tonight and he noted that
even through the COVID-19 pandemic, the City improved its funded position from 75.6% to 76.9%
which is extraordinary during this time. He complimented Director of Administrative Services
Cheryl Dyas and her staff for that accomplishment. Council Member Sachs noted that the 5-year
amortization rate that CalPers is using has been great for the pension liability. And lastly, he
discussed a former Council Member's accusation that the Council violated the Brown Act and he
outlined some questionable incidents that occurred when the same individual served on the City
Council.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley supported Council Member Sachs recollection and stated that she was on
the dais when one questionable incident took place with the former Council Member. She shared
City Council Minutes  9  August 25, 2020
 that she took her grandchildren to Menchie’s Frozen Yogurt and spoke with the owner, Isabelle,
who indicated that her business is down about 50%. Council Member Kelley expressed her concern
for businesses and reminded residents to support Mission Viejo establishments. She also noted that
staff members have been very proactive collecting food at drive-through drives and providing the
food to South County Outreach, Families Forward and Family Assistance Ministries. The next food
drives will be August 29, September 26, and October 24 at Norman P. Murray Community Center
from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. She also noted that Saddleback Church will be hosting a food
distribution event on September 5 at Newhart Middle School and they plan to continue this outreach
in October, November and December at various locations. Council Member Kelley warned
residents that during the current heat wave, electric bills will be high. And finally, she commented
on her son and daughter-in-law conducting remote learning and the challenges that both teachers
and parents are facing.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell announced that he is involved with the Orange County Mayors in a campaign to
encourage people to wear masks and to pitch in so children can get back to school and sports. In
this effort, he filmed a public service announcement at the new Saddleback College stadium along
with Mayors from Rancho Santa Margarita, Lake Forest, and the Mayor Pro Tem from San
Clemente. Mayor Goodell encouraged residents to get tested for COVID-19. He also announced
that he is working with staff and some Community Services Commissioners to explore the idea of
creating a committee on inclusiveness in response to a lot of concerns that he is hearing within the
community. He stated that he hopes there will be a formal plan that he can present to the Council
at the next meeting and appoint a committee, including members of the public. Mayor Goodell
announced that in September there will be an update on the I-5 Widening Project and an OCTA
grant that will provide money to build a sound wall along the freeway from Oso Parkway to the
south end of Mission Viejo High School. Lastly, he stated that he was saddened at the news that
Stein Mart is bankrupt and will be going out of business.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:06 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 8, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 8, 2020

City Council Minutes  10  August 25, 2020
